data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Xanthine oxidase inhibitor

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits xanthine oxidase → lowers uric acid; also inhibits Leishmania purine salvage (allopurinol riboside is toxic to parasite)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Gout and tophi; prevention of tumour lysis
- Dermatology (off-label, historic): cutaneous leishmaniasis (with antimonials), sarcoidosis, reactive perforating collagenosis, granuloma annulare

## Dose & formulations
- 100–300 mg/day (start low, especially in renal impairment)

## Adverse effects
- Severe cutaneous adverse reactions: DRESS, SJS/TEN — allopurinol is the commonest cause of SJS/TEN in many countries; strongly linked to HLA-B*58:01 (screen in Han Chinese, Korean, Thai patients)
- Rash, hepatitis, interstitial nephritis, vasculitis

## Contraindications
- Previous allopurinol hypersensitivity; HLA-B*58:01 positive (if tested)

## Drug interactions
- Azathioprine/6-mercaptopurine: severe myelosuppression — reduce azathioprine to 25% or avoid
- Ampicillin/amoxicillin: more rash; thiazides (hypersensitivity); cyclophosphamide (marrow toxicity)

## Monitoring
- Renal function (start low), CBC, LFT; warn about rash in the first 8 weeks

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid unless essential.

## Viva points
- Top cause of SJS/TEN and DRESS — HLA-B*58:01
- Allopurinol + azathioprine = severe marrow suppression

_Sources: Khopkar (Allopurinol); Wolverton 4e ch.66 and ch.67. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
